sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Franklin County?
sections.html:
The county's Tax Office is split into the Assessor's Office, the Collections Department and GIS/Mapping, and its phone is 919-496-2172. When call volume is heavy, expect voicemail.

The assessor lists and values real estate, personal property and registered motor vehicles. The collector works under the Machinery Act and pursues current and delinquent accounts. Value questions go to the Tax Assessor's Office, P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549, while payments and certification requests go to the Tax Collector, P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549.

The county is adding residents quickly. The Census Bureau shows 82,037 people on July 1, 2025 against 68,625 at the April 2020 base, a 19.5 percent jump, spread over 491.80 square miles of land. Owners occupy 78.6 percent of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $284,300, and 735 building permits were issued in 2025. Workers average 33.3 minutes getting to their jobs.

sections.h2: What is the due date on a Franklin County bill?
sections.html:
Each year's tax is due September 1 and turns delinquent after January 5, so the 2026 bills go delinquent on January 6, 2027.

Bills come out in late July or early August. Payment before September 1 earns a discount, and prepaying before the bills are produced is allowed. After the delinquency date the county moves to enforced collection, and G.S. 105-360 adds 2 percent from January 6 to February 1, then three-fourths of one percent for each month or part of one.

Cards are processed by a third party, BIS Online Services, for a non-refundable convenience fee, at 877-768-4775 by phone. A caller needs the tax year, bill number, local zip code and amount; the county office at 919-496-2172 can supply the figure. A past-due notice sometimes crosses with a payment in the mail, so pay ahead of the deadline and include interest if late.

Escrow customers can verify their lender's payment in the second week of September, as the next section explains, and anyone selling should ask the Collections Department for a current balance before setting a closing date.

sections.h2: Why does a Franklin County bill arrive when the lender escrows?
sections.html:
The county mails every bill to the owner of record, and lenders then pick out the ones they are responsible for from a county file.

To confirm the lender paid, search the county's collection site in the second week of September or call 919-496-2172 and choose option 2. The county suggests sending a copy of the bill to the mortgage company with the next house payment. A seller who has already closed should forward the bill to the new owner unless the seller means to pay it. The county treats side agreements among buyers, sellers and attorneys as outside its concern, but because the tax is a lien, a buyer wants each bill settled before closing.

sections.h2: What is the Franklin County tax certification step?
sections.html:
A deed that transfers real property cannot be registered in Franklin County until the Tax Collector certifies that no delinquent tax is a lien on the parcel, a rule in place since April 1, 2015.

Collections issues the stamp at no charge on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., except county holidays, and a closing attorney or seller can walk in before recording. Mailed requests go to the Tax Collector, P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549, with the words Attention: Tax Certification. Electronic filings pass through the certification step automatically.

For a seller, an open bill can hold up registration of the deed. If the current bill is unpaid, pay it directly or have the closing agent pay from proceeds so the certification can issue.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Franklin County assessment?
sections.html:
A real estate appeal may be filed any time after January 1 until the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns, usually in May, or within 30 days of a value change notice.

Values rest on the January 1, 2024 revaluation. The county wants the appeal form returned, with all supporting papers, to Franklin County Revaluation, P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549, before April. Staff review comes first. When that fails, a hearing before the board is scheduled and a decision is mailed. Anything filed after adjournment waits for the next tax year. A further step goes to the state Property Tax Commission within 30 days of the board's notice, and the owner carries the burden of showing a substantial overstatement.

How the Franklin County Tax Office sorts appeal reasons (source: county Value Appeals page)
Reason offeredCounty position
Bill is higher than before, or income is fixed in retirementNo legal basis
Prices fell or you paid less after January 1, 2024No legal basis under G.S. 105-287
Similar homes carry lower assessed valuesHas a legal basis
Highly similar sales before January 1, 2024 at far lower pricesHas a legal basis
Fire, wind or water damage still unrepaired on January 1Has a legal basis, with proof and photos
Septic permit denied, with a Health Department letterHas a legal basis

sections.h2: Is there relief for Franklin County homeowners on a fixed income?
sections.html:
Three state programs exist and an owner can use just one: the senior or disability exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker.

  • Senior or disabled owners with income at or below the 2026 ceiling of $38,800 shield at least $25,000 of value, or half the value if that is more.
  • Disabled veterans shield $45,000 of value with no age or income test.
  • The circuit breaker holds tax to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent between $38,800 and $58,200, for owners who have lived in the home five years, and defers the excess.

Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor, not the state revenue department. The county's appeals page sends retirees to the Tax Assessor's Office for relief questions, since a fixed income does not lower the value itself. A sale triggers repayment of any circuit breaker deferral.

sections.h2: Do Franklin County fees and liens affect a sale?
sections.html:
Yes: a solid waste availability fee rides on bills for any dwelling or business with an electrical hookup, and the tax is a lien on the parcel.

The county says the fee pays for collection and disposal at twelve convenience centers, applies per electrical connection and does not depend on full-time residence, so a vacant house with power still carries it. Commissioners set the amount each year in the budget ordinance, so ask the Tax Office for the figure on your parcel.

If a bill goes unpaid, G.S. 105-355 attaches the lien as of the listing date and G.S. 105-374 lets the county foreclose it in court through a courthouse-door sale and a 10-day window for increased bids. A bankruptcy filer still gets bills, though the collector cannot pursue delinquent tax during the case.

Owners who inherit a house with back taxes face the same lien as any seller. The tax collector can supply the open years, and G.S. 105-374 lets a redeeming person clear the debt before the court confirms a sale by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

faqs.q: On what date do 2026 Franklin County bills go delinquent?
faqs.a: January 6, 2027, according to the Collections page. The September 1 due date applies to all real estate and personal property bills.

faqs.q: Will Franklin County record my deed without a tax certification?
faqs.a: No. The Register of Deeds takes a transfer deed only after the Tax Collector certifies no delinquent tax lien. The certification is free on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

faqs.q: Where does a Franklin County value appeal go?
faqs.a: To P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549 on the Board of Equalization and Review form with supporting papers. File after January 1 and before the board adjourns, or within 30 days of a value change notice.

faqs.q: Does a larger bill justify a lower Franklin County value?
faqs.a: No, the county lists a higher bill or fixed income as having no legal basis. Stronger proof is similar properties with lower values, pre-2024 sales or documented damage.

faqs.q: What number do I use to check or pay a Franklin County bill?
faqs.a: Call 919-496-2172 and choose option 2 to check payments. Card payments by phone go through BIS Online Services at 877-768-4775, with a convenience fee.
